new.title: Climb the Karlsturm of the Grossmünster
new.desc: The twin-towered Romanesque Grossmünster was the centre of Huldrych Zwingli's Reformation in Zurich, and tradition links its founding to Charlemagne. The Karlsturm can be climbed up around 187 steps for a view over the old town, the Limmat and the lake.
new.tip: Entry to the church is free; the tower climb costs a few francs. Go on a clear morning for the best view.

new.title: See Chagall's blue windows in the Fraumünster
new.desc: Marc Chagall designed five tall stained-glass windows for the choir of the Fraumünster, each with its own colour and biblical theme, from the Jacob window to the Christ window. The church also holds glass by Augusto Giacometti.
new.tip: Light is best on bright mornings. Photography is restricted inside, and a small colour brochure on the windows is sold at the entrance.

new.title: Stand under the giant clock of St. Peter
new.desc: St. Peter is the oldest parish church in Zurich, and its tower carries the largest church clock face in Europe, with a dial about 8.7 metres across. The tower belongs to the city and served as a fire watch until 1911.
new.tip: The best view of the dial is from the lane beside the church. Inside, the nave is free to enter.
new.q: Kirche St. Peter, St. Peterhofstatt 1, Altstadt, Zürich

new.title: Spend an afternoon at the Kunsthaus Zürich
new.desc: The Chipperfield extension opened in October 2021 and made the Kunsthaus Switzerland's largest art museum. It shows classic modernism, the Bührle collection of Impressionists, and postwar art, linked to the old building by an underground passage.
new.tip: Open Tuesday to Sunday and late on Thursday. Allow two to three hours, and note that one room contextualises the Bührle collection's history.

new.title: Explore Swiss history in the Landesmuseum
new.desc: The Swiss National Museum, founded in 1898, occupies Gustav Gull's castle-like building beside the main station, joined by a modern extension by Christ & Gantenbein. Its permanent exhibitions run from prehistoric archaeology through Swiss cultural and art history.
new.tip: Closed on Mondays. Combine it with a walk through Platzspitz park behind the building.

new.title: Wander the Rieterpark and Museum Rietberg
new.desc: The Museum Rietberg is Switzerland's museum for non-European art, built around the collection of Baron Eduard von der Heydt and opened in 1952 in the neoclassical Villa Wesendonck, once home to Otto and Mathilde Wesendonck, friends of Richard Wagner. It also includes the Schönberg villa and a modern pavilion in Rieterpark.
new.tip: Open Tuesday to Sunday. The park around the villa is free and has old trees and lake views.

new.title: Hold football history at the FIFA Museum
new.desc: The FIFA Museum opened on 28 February 2016 in the renovated Haus zur Enge beside Enge station. Three floors show more than 1,000 objects on football and the World Cup, including the original trophy.
new.tip: Open Tuesday to Sunday. Tram 7 and the S-Bahn stop at Bahnhof Enge, next door.

new.title: Step inside Le Corbusier's last building
new.desc: The Pavillon Le Corbusier on the Zürichhorn was completed in 1967, the architect's last building, and is made of enamelled steel and glass. Run since 2019 by the Museum für Gestaltung for the city, it shows his work and ideas.
new.tip: Seasonal: open roughly April to late November, closed in winter. Free on Thursday evenings from 17:00.
new.q: Pavillon Le Corbusier, Höschgasse 8, Seefeld, Zürich

new.title: Look over the old town from the Lindenhof
new.desc: The Lindenhof hill was the core of Roman Turicum, founded around 15 BC, and later the site of a Carolingian palace. Under its lime trees you get a view of the Limmat, the Grossmünster and, on clear days, the Alps.
new.tip: Free and quiet in the morning. Locals play oversized chess here in the afternoon.

new.title: See Zurich West from the Prime Tower
new.desc: The 126-metre Prime Tower in the former Maag industrial area was Switzerland's tallest building when completed. The Clouds restaurant and bar on the 35th floor looks over Zürich-West and the rooftops.
new.tip: Only the restaurant floor is open to the public, so book a table or visit for a drink. Zürich Hardbrücke station is a short walk.
new.q: Prime Tower, Hardstrasse 201, Zürich West, Zürich

new.title: Visit Cabaret Voltaire, birthplace of Dada
new.desc: Hugo Ball and Emmy Hennings opened Cabaret Voltaire at Spiegelgasse 1 in February 1916 in the back room of the Holländische Meierei tavern. The performances there started the Dada movement; the building was revived as a cultural venue in the 21st century.
new.tip: Small exhibition space with a bar; check opening days, as hours vary with the programme.

new.title: Stroll the Chinese Garden on the Zürichhorn
new.desc: The Chinagarten was a gift from Zurich's partner city Kunming and was built in 1993. It is a temple-style garden of pavilions, ponds and bridges on the Zürichhorn shore, close to Tinguely's kinetic sculpture Heureka.
new.tip: Small entrance fee; open in the warmer months. Combine with the lakeside promenade and the Le Corbusier pavilion next door.

new.title: Spot the Guardian Angel in Zurich main station
new.desc: Niki de Saint Phalle's colourful sculpture L'ange protecteur hangs in the station hall. It is about 11 metres tall, weighs 1.2 tonnes and has hung from steel cables since November 1997, a gift from Securitas for the 150th anniversary of Swiss railways.
new.tip: Free, right in the main hall. Mario Merz's neon spiral installation is in the same hall.

new.title: Browse posters at the Museum für Gestaltung
new.desc: Zurich's design museum keeps more than 500,000 objects, including one of the world's largest poster collections. The listed Ausstellungsstrasse building hosts exhibitions, with a poster display marking the museum's 150th anniversary in 2025.
new.tip: Open Tuesday to Sunday, late on Thursday; closed Monday. The collection depot is at Toni-Areal.

new.title: Admire the Baroque Rathaus and Wasserkirche
new.desc: The Rathaus on the Limmat was built in 1694 to 1698 and still houses the city and cantonal parliaments. Beside it stands the Wasserkirche, rebuilt in 1479 to 1484 on a former island, next to the Helmhaus.
new.tip: Walk the Limmatquai quay, which has been traffic-free since 2004. Council sessions are open to the public on some days.

new.title: Rest in the Old Botanical Garden
new.desc: The Alter Botanischer Garten sits on the former Bollwerk zur Katz bastion beside the Schanzengraben. Zurich's first botanical garden dates to 1746, and the university ran its botanical research here until 1976.
new.tip: Free and closes at dusk. Pelikanstrasse is a short walk from Bahnhofstrasse and Sihlstrasse.

new.title: Find James Joyce's grave at Friedhof Fluntern
new.desc: James Joyce was buried at Friedhof Fluntern on 15 January 1941, and a bronze statue now marks his honorary grave. Nobel laureate Elias Canetti lies nearby, and the zoo next door means lions can be heard from Joyce's resting place.
new.tip: Free; tram 6 to the Zoo terminus. Joyce's grave is signposted from the main path.

new.title: Visit the Freitag container tower
new.desc: The Freitag flagship store is a tower of 19 shipping containers, around 25 metres high, opened in 2006 and made permanent in 2014. The shop sells bags made from recycled truck tarpaulins, with a viewing terrace on top.
new.tip: Closed Sundays. Quick to combine with Frau Gerolds Garten across the road.
new.q: Freitag Flagship Store, Geroldstrasse 17, Zürich West, Zürich

new.title: See contemporary art at the Löwenbräukunst
new.desc: The former Löwenbräu brewery from 1897 now holds the Migros Museum für Gegenwartskunst, founded in 1996, next to the Kunsthalle and galleries such as Hauser & Wirth. It is one of the main addresses for current art in Zurich West.
new.tip: Open Tuesday to Sunday, late on Thursday. Check whether admission is free on your visit.
new.q: Migros Museum für Gegenwartskunst, Limmatstrasse 270, Zürich

new.title: Admire the Opernhaus on Sechseläutenplatz
new.desc: The Zürich Opera House was built in 1890 to 1891 by Fellner and Helmer after the earlier Aktientheater burned down, and opened on 1 October 1891. It is home to the Zurich Opera and Ballet and was named Opera Company of the Year at the 2014 International Opera Awards.
new.tip: Standing-room and last-minute tickets are often cheap; the facade is lit nicely in the evening.

new.title: Walk the Bahnhofstrasse to Paradeplatz
new.desc: The Bahnhofstrasse was opened in stages from 1865, and Jelmoli became the first department store here on 16 September 1899. It runs from the station to the lake, past banks and the Grieder-Haus at Paradeplatz.
new.tip: Walk it from the station down to Bürkliplatz. Shops close early on Saturday and Sunday.

new.title: Wander the Niederdorf alleys and Rindermarkt
new.desc: The Niederdorf is the lower part of the medieval old town, with narrow lanes such as Spiegelgasse and Napfgasse. At Rindermarkt 9 the novelist Gottfried Keller once lived, and some of Zurich's last gas street lamps are here.
new.tip: Pedestrian zone, lively at night. Daytime is calmer for photographs.

new.title: Shop under the railway arches at Im Viadukt
new.desc: Im Viadukt turns the brick arches of a viaduct built in 1894 into boutiques, design shops and cafés, with a covered market hall. It is one of the best-known reuses of old industrial structures in Zürich-West.
new.tip: Shops mostly open Monday to Saturday and close Sundays. Zürich Hardbrücke station is a short walk.

new.title: Catch a gig at the Rote Fabrik on the lake
new.desc: The Rote Fabrik is a former silk factory from 1892 on the lake shore in Wollishofen. Voters saved it from demolition in 1977 and it became a cultural centre with concert halls, a theatre and a lakeside restaurant.
new.tip: Bus 161 or 165 stops at the door. Programme varies, so check what is on; the lake terrace is a good place for a summer evening.

new.title: Walk through the Masoala Rainforest at Zoo Zürich
new.desc: Zoo Zürich lies on the Zürichberg and its Masoala hall recreates the rainforest of a Madagascar peninsula in about 10,000 square metres. The hall opened in 2003 and a treetop walkway has been open since 2013.
new.tip: Tram 6 to Zoo. The hall opens around 10:00; plan about three hours for the whole zoo.

new.title: Climb the Uto Kulm tower on the Uetliberg
new.desc: The Uetliberg is Zurich's local mountain, and at its summit the Uto Kulm viewing tower rises 72 metres. The platform looks over the city, the lake and the Alps.
new.tip: Reach the Uetliberg by S10 train in about 30 minutes, then walk ten minutes to the summit. Clear days in autumn and winter are best.

new.title: Dine among Chagall and Miró at the Kronenhalle
new.desc: The Kronenhalle at Bellevue is a classic Zurich brasserie hung with works by Chagall, Miró, Picasso and Matisse, collected by the Zumsteg family. Miró was a friend of the family and Chagall called himself a surrogate son.
new.tip: Order the Zürcher Geschnetzeltes. Reserve ahead and expect high prices.

new.title: Eat sausages at the Zeughauskeller
new.desc: The Zeughauskeller is a former armoury on Bahnhofstrasse that has been a restaurant for about a century. It serves Swiss sausage dishes and rösti in a hall decorated with old weapons.
new.tip: Order a sausage with rösti, such as the house Bürgermeister-Schwert. Book ahead, as it fills up.

new.title: Taste Luxemburgerli at Sprüngli on Paradeplatz
new.desc: Confiserie Sprüngli opened on Paradeplatz in 1859 and the Luxemburgerli macaron arrived in 1957. The café and shop remain one of Zurich's best-known sweet stops.
new.tip: Buy Luxemburgerli by the piece; they are best eaten the same day. The café upstairs serves hot chocolate and cakes.

new.title: Fill a plate at Haus Hiltl, the world's oldest vegetarian restaurant
new.desc: Haus Hiltl was founded in 1898 by Ambrosius Hiltl and is recognised by Guinness as the oldest vegetarian restaurant in the world. Its buffet offers over 100 dishes, priced by the weight of the plate.
new.tip: Choose from the buffet and have your plate weighed. Prices are on the higher side.

new.title: Grab a Bratwurst at Sternen Grill
new.desc: Sternen Grill at Bellevue is known for its St. Galler Bratwurst served with a golden Bürli bread roll and sharp house mustard. It has been a late-night and lunch-hour stop since the 1960s.
new.tip: Order the Bratwurst with Bürli and mustard; the mustard is hot. Hours differ by day, so check.

new.title: Order Zürcher Geschnetzeltes at Zunfthaus zur Waag
new.desc: The Zunfthaus zur Waag is a guild house near the Fraumünster, now a restaurant known for Zürcher Geschnetzeltes with rösti. The veal and cream mushroom sauce is a slow, all-day preparation.
new.tip: Reserve a table; the dish is on the menu all year.

new.title: Eat Zürigschnätzlets at Zum Kropf
new.desc: Zum Kropf on In Gassen is a historic beer hall dating to around 1880 with ceiling frescoes, wood panelling and stained glass. It serves Zürigschnätzlets with rösti and draught beer.
new.tip: It is near Paradeplatz and the Zeughauskeller. Expect a traditional crowd at lunch.
new.q: Restaurant zum Kropf, In Gassen 16, Zürich

new.title: Drink beer at the Rheinfelder Bierhaus
new.desc: The Rheinfelder Bierhaus on Marktgasse, nicknamed De bluetig Duume, is a rustic Niederdorf beer hall serving hearty Swiss food. Zürcher Geschnetzeltes with rösti, pork liver and cordon bleu are regulars on the menu.
new.tip: Waiters have a gruff charm. Check which of the Rheinfelder halls you want, as there are two similarly named ones.

new.title: Share a fondue at Swiss Chuchi
new.desc: The Swiss Chuchi in Hotel Adler in the Niederdorf has served cheese specialities since 1953. The menu centres on the Adler special fondue, raclette and Vaud fondue, plus Älplermagronen and Capuns.
new.tip: Reserve a table in winter. Prices are on the higher side.

new.title: Sip hot chocolate at Conditorei Schober
new.desc: On Napfgasse since 1842, the confectioner Theodor Schober took over in 1874; the café is now called 1842 Café & Confiserie. Guides rate its hot chocolate with cream among the best in Zurich.
new.tip: Weekends can mean a wait, and tables are not reserved. Order the hot chocolate with a pastry.

new.title: Have coffee in the Art Nouveau Café Odeon
new.desc: Café Odeon opened in 1911 on Limmatquai in the style of a Viennese coffeehouse. Lenin and other intellectuals reportedly met here, and James Joyce is documented as a regular during his Zurich years.
new.tip: Come for coffee in the afternoon or a cocktail in the evening. The bar stays open late.

new.title: Drink under the arches at Frau Gerolds Garten
new.desc: Frau Gerolds Garten is an outdoor bar, restaurant and urban garden built from shipping containers on Geroldstrasse, open since 2012. In winter a large wooden shack with a fireplace goes up.
new.tip: Hours change by season; summer evenings get busy. Pair it with a visit to the Freitag tower.

new.title: Dine at Clouds on the 35th floor of the Prime Tower
new.desc: Clouds is a bar and restaurant on the 35th floor of the Prime Tower, around 120 metres up, with an open kitchen and Catalan-inspired food. Time Out rates it 4 out of 5 stars.
new.tip: Book a window table for sunset. There is a vegetarian tasting menu.

new.title: Taste award-winning coffee at Miró in Kreis 4
new.desc: Miró Coffee on Brauerstrasse was named Switzerland's Roaster of the Year in 2025 by The Way to Coffee. It is part of the dense specialty-coffee scene of Kreis 4 and 5.
new.tip: Try a filter coffee. Kreis 4 side streets such as Brauerstrasse are calmer than Langstrasse.

new.title: Sip a cocktail at the Jules Verne Panoramabar
new.desc: Jules Verne is a rooftop panoramic bar at Schoeneggstrasse 25 near Langstrasse, listed among the area's notable bars. Guides advise booking for sunset.
new.tip: Reserve for sunset; walk in only after 22:00.

new.title: Dine in a guild hall at Zunfthaus zum Rüden
new.desc: The Zunfthaus zum Rüden is a historic Limmatquai guild house now run as a restaurant. A recent reviewer calls its Zürcher Geschnetzeltes some of the best in the city.
new.tip: Reserve ahead; it is formal and priced accordingly.

new.title: Dine at the guild house Zunfthaus zur Zimmerleuten
new.desc: The Zunfthaus zur Zimmerleuten on Limmatquai is one of Zurich's historic guild houses, now a restaurant serving Swiss classics. A zuri.net reviewer calls its Zürcher Geschnetzeltes the best in town, though other reviews are mixed.
new.tip: Check recent reviews and reserve ahead.

new.title: Have a drink at the Barfussbar in the Frauenbadi
new.desc: The Barfussbar has been inside the Frauenbad Stadthausquai, a floating wooden river bath, since 1997. By day the bath is women-only, but in the evening everyone can come for a drink on the Limmat.
new.tip: Open in the warm months only; take off your shoes at the entrance.

new.title: Swim at Seebad Utoquai in the Badepalast
new.desc: The Seebad Utoquai is a wooden lake bath in Moorish style built in 1890 by William Henri Marti, the first Zurich bath allowing men and women together. It has a diving board, rafts, small pools and a sauna.
new.tip: Open in summer. Bring a towel; the water is lakewater in the Seefeld, about ten minutes' walk from Bellevue.

new.title: Float in the women-only Frauenbadi
new.desc: The Frauenbad Stadthausquai is a floating wooden Kastenbad on the Limmat at Bürkliplatz, built in 1887 or 1888 after a city decision of 1837. It is reserved for women in the daytime.
new.tip: Open in summer; women only by day. Free swimming in the river outside the bath is not allowed.

new.title: Swim in summer or sauna in winter at Seebad Enge
new.desc: Seebad Enge on Mythenquai was built in 1959 to 1960 by Robert Landolt in the style of the wooden box baths. Outside the swimming season its sauna overlooks the lake, and you can jump into the cold water after.
new.tip: Sauna season runs late September to early May, with Monday for women only. Check opening times by phone.

new.title: Float down the Limmat at Oberer Letten
new.desc: Flussbad Oberer Letten is a river bath near the main station with a 400-metre swimming channel and a 2-metre diving platform. In summer it is one of the busiest meeting points on the river.
new.tip: Open in summer; walk about five minutes from the main station. Check river conditions and the summer opening hours.

new.title: Swim at Strandbad Tiefenbrunnen
new.desc: Strandbad Tiefenbrunnen is a park-set lake bath on the right shore next to the Zürichhorn. It opened in 1886, has diving platforms at 1, 3 and 5 metres, and a long water slide.
new.tip: Open in summer; check current admission. A stand-up paddle board rental machine is on site.

new.title: Cruise Lake Zurich from Bürkliplatz
new.desc: The ZSG lake boats leave from the Bürkliplatz landing stage. A short loop of about an hour and a half runs around the inner lake basin to the Zürichhorn.
new.tip: The service is covered by the Swiss Travel Pass and the Zurich day ticket on the zones. Sit on the open deck on a clear day.

new.title: Ride a paddle steamer to Rapperswil
new.desc: Lake Zurich's two remaining steam paddle ships are the Stadt Zürich (1909) and the Stadt Rapperswil (1914), the latter a Class A cultural property. The long lake round trip to Rapperswil takes about four and a half hours.
new.tip: Steamers mostly run on Sundays in summer. Check the ZSG timetable before you plan.

new.title: Drift down the Limmat on a river boat
new.desc: Limmat boats run from the pier by the Landesmuseum near the main station through the old town to Bürkliplatz, with stops such as Limmatquai and Storchen. It is a quick way to see the old town from the water.
new.tip: Seasonal service, mainly spring to autumn; check the timetable.

new.title: Hike the Planet Path on the Uetliberg
new.desc: The Planetenweg on the Uetliberg is a scale model of the solar system at 1 to 1 billion. The ridge route continues to Uto Kulm and on to Felsenegg.
new.tip: Take the S10 to Uetliberg station. Wear good shoes, as the ridge has steep steps and loose gravel.

new.title: Ride the Polybahn up to the ETH terrace
new.desc: The Polybahn funicular has linked Central square with the Polyterrasse of ETH Zurich since 1889, a ride of about 100 seconds. The free terrace looks over the old town, the Limmat and the lake.
new.tip: Covered by Zurich public transport tickets. Go on a clear day for the Alps.

new.title: Take the Dolderbahn up the Adlisberg
new.desc: The Dolderbahn is a 1.3 km rack railway from Römerhof to the Dolder Grand hotel and Dolder recreation area. It opened in 1895 as a funicular and was converted to rack operation in 1973.
new.tip: Take tram 3 or 8 to Römerhof, then the Dolderbahn. Combine it with a walk in the Adlisberg woods.

new.title: Browse the Bürkliplatz flea market
new.desc: The Bürkliplatz flea market runs on Saturdays from early May to late October on the lake, with over 200 seasonal stalls selling antiques, vintage items and second-hand goods.
new.tip: Hours vary by source, roughly 7:00 to 17:00. Come early for the best finds.

new.title: Shop the Saturday market in Oerlikon
new.desc: Marktplatz Oerlikon hosts a local market on Saturdays from 6:00 to 12:00. Oerlikon is also home to the Hallenstadion and MFO-Park, a park built in a steel framework on a former engine factory site.
new.tip: Closed on Sundays. Combine with a walk through MFO-Park.

new.title: Visit the Christmas village at Sechseläutenplatz
new.desc: The main Zurich Christmas market, with around 100 stalls, is in front of the Opera House. Further markets run in the old town, at the main station and at Münsterhof.
new.tip: Runs from late November to late December; evenings are busiest.

new.title: Watch the Böögg burn at Sechseläuten
new.desc: Sechseläuten is Zurich's spring festival, held on the third Monday of April, ending with the burning of the Böögg, a snowman stuffed with fireworks. The faster his head explodes, the better the summer is said to be.
new.tip: A guild parade runs the day before. Arrive early for a view of Sechseläutenplatz.

new.title: Dance at the Street Parade
new.desc: The Street Parade is held on the second Saturday of August and is described as the largest techno party in the world, with more than a million people. The route runs along the lake from Utoquai to the Enge harbour.
new.tip: Expect very crowded trams and closed roads. Sunscreen and water are a must.

new.title: Cycle the Zürichsee path from Mythenquai
new.desc: The Zürichsee cycle path rings the lake in about 61 km with only modest climbing. A short section along Mythenquai is an easy introduction from the city.
new.tip: Rent a Züri Velo bike from PubliBike, or borrow a free city bike with ID and deposit via ZüriRollt.
